subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should the `read` tool get a narrow binary-document fallback now, or should this wait for broader document parsing/provider-native file work?
rationale: Current source still has the token-waste path, but the issue proposes multiple product shapes and the only open linked implementation is conflicting and stale against the current read-tool layout.

options.title: Land narrow fallback
options.body: Replace or repair the linked guard in the current read path so known PDF/Office documents return a clear unsupported/document-tool message while preserving text and image reads.

options.title: Fold into document architecture
options.body: Keep this issue as context for the broader document extraction/provider-native file design and do not add a read-specific fallback yet.

recommendation.title: Land narrow fallback
recommendation.body: Replace or repair the linked guard in the current read path so known PDF/Office documents return a clear unsupported/document-tool message while preserving text and image reads.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest read-wrapper history signal points to Peter Steinberger's tool split and read-wrapper refactors.
